name: Bottom nav
description: A phone app's tab bar: three to five top-level destinations, each an icon over a short label, pinned to the bottom of the screen within thumb reach and clear of the home indicator.

classes.ayy-bottom-nav: The <nav>. Equal-width columns, one per link. Sticky to the bottom of its scroll container (the page, or the box it scrolls in), with the safe-area inset added below.
classes.ayy-bottom-nav__link: Destination link: icon over label. aria-current="page" marks the page you're on: a pill behind the icon and a heavier label.
classes.ayy-bottom-nav__label: The link's text, one line, cut with an ellipsis if it's too long.

BottomNavLink.renders: <a class="ayy-bottom-nav__link"> with the icon and a <span class="ayy-bottom-nav__label">

props.icon: ReactNode — the icon above the label (an <Icon>).

a11y: It's a <nav>: give it an aria-label ("Main" by default in React). If the app also has a sidebar or drawer with the same links, show only one of them at a time.
Mark the current page with aria-current="page". It also gets a pill and a heavier weight, so colour isn't the only cue; High Contrast mode fills the pill with the system highlight.
Every link keeps a visible text label. Icon-only tabs are guesswork.
Each link is at least the large control height, so it's a comfortable touch target at every density.
Content above it needs bottom padding (or to end before it) so the last line isn't hidden behind the bar.
do: Use a bottom nav for the three to five top-level destinations of a phone app, so they're one thumb-tap away.
Keep labels to one short word: Home, Search, Inbox, Account.
Show it on phones only and switch to the App shell sidebar on wider screens (hide it from 48rem with a media query).
Use the same icons as the sidebar for the same destinations.
dont: Don't use a bottom nav for actions (compose, share) — use a Button, or a bottom-sheet Dialog for a list of actions.
Don't use it to switch views of one thing inside a page — use Tabs.
Don't put more than five links in it; put the rest in a drawer (App shell with a bar) or on an Account page.
Don't nest menus in it or change its links from page to page.
